report:
## Conclusion

Yes — current evidence suggests olive leaf extract (OLE), particularly its main polyphenol oleuropein, can modestly lower blood pressure, especially in people with prehypertension or mild (stage-1) hypertension, though it is not a substitute for prescribed antihypertensive therapy in more severe cases.

**Key evidence:**
- A double-blind RCT by Susalit et al. compared OLE (500 mg twice daily) to Captopril in stage-1 hypertensive patients and found OLE produced comparable reductions in systolic and diastolic blood pressure, with additional favorable effects on lipids and good tolerability ([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21036583](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21036583/)).
- A crossover trial in prehypertensive mono-zygotic twins found that a phenolic-rich OLE (providing 136 mg/day oleuropein) significantly reduced both systolic and diastolic blood pressure compared to placebo, alongside improvements in cholesterol ([link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00394-016-1188-y](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00394-016-1188-y)).
- A more recent systematic review and meta-analysis (2022) found OLE significantly reduced systolic blood pressure across pooled trials, though effects on diastolic pressure were less consistent and some individual comparisons (e.g., 1,000 mg/day combination formulas vs. placebo) showed no significant difference ([researchgate.net/publication/358844735](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/358844735_The_Effect_of_Olive_Leaf_Extract_on_Systolic_and_Diastolic_Blood_Pressure_in_Adults_A_Systemic_Review_and_Meta-Analysis)).
- A 2025 systematic review/meta-analysis specifically in pre-hypertensive and hypertensive adults reaffirmed a beneficial effect on blood pressure, suggesting OLE could be a safe adjunct or alternative for milder cases ([researchgate.net/publication/391485868](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/391485868_Efficacy_of_Olive_Leaf_Extract_in_Improving_Blood_Pressure_in_Pre-Hypertensive_and_Hypertensive_Individuals_A_Systematic_Review_and_Meta-Analysis)).

**Caveats:** Effect sizes vary by dose, formulation, and duration; most trials are small to moderate in size. Anyone with diagnosed hypertension should consult a physician before replacing or combining medications with OLE, since it may potentiate antihypertensive drug effects.
